title: Chiranjit Das
text: I am an independent researcher working on remote sensing and inversion methodologies to understand the distribution of atmosphere-biosphere-ocean CO2 fluxes. My work sits at the intersection of satellite observation, atmospheric modeling, and carbon cycle science, aiming to close gaps in how we observe and attribute greenhouse gas sources and sinks at regional and global scales.

title: Research
text:
My research focuses on quantifying and understanding CO2 fluxes across the atmosphere-biosphere-ocean system, combining satellite remote sensing with inverse modeling techniques.


I use satellite-derived trace gas retrievals together with atmospheric transport and inversion frameworks to estimate surface CO2 fluxes and constrain their spatial and temporal distribution.
Add details: instruments/datasets used (e.g., OCO-2, OCO-3, GOSAT, TROPOMI), inversion frameworks, and key findings.



Investigating the drivers of terrestrial and oceanic carbon uptake and release, and how these processes respond to climate variability.



Studying the regional-scale distribution and variability of CO2, CH4, and N2O, and their links to land-use, emissions, and natural sink/source processes.



Examining feedbacks between the carbon cycle and the climate system, and how these interactions shape projections of future warming.
